# robots.txt - immovlan.be (production)
#
# Structure:
#   1. Sitemap
#   2. Site-wide crawl policy (User-agent: * plus the AI crawlers that share it)
#   3. Googlebot-News (news content only)
#   4. AI crawlers we turn away
#   5. Legacy scrapers and offline-copy tools we turn away
#
# Every rule below is a Disallow on the site-wide group unless stated otherwise.
# Groups do not inherit from each other in robots.txt, so an agent that should
# get the normal policy is added as an extra User-agent line on the group in
# section 2 rather than repeated in a group of its own.
#
# Editing rules:
#   - Patterns are case-sensitive. A path blocked in two casings needs two lines.
#   - Prefer an anchored pattern (/nl/foo*) over a bare substring (*foo*).
#     Bare substrings match anywhere in the path and cause collateral damage.
#   - Matching runs over the path AND the query string, so a rule anchored with
#     $ stops firing as soon as a parameter is appended. Pair it with a '?' rule.
#   - Anything advertised in llms.txt must stay crawlable. Immovlan.Website.Tests
#     LlmsTxtIntegrityTests.NoAdvertisedUrlIsDisallowedByRobots enforces this for
#     the site-wide group and fails the build on drift.

Sitemap: https://immovlan.be/sitemap.xml

# =============================================================================
# 2. Site-wide crawl policy
# =============================================================================
# The AI agents listed here get exactly the same policy as every other crawler:
# everything except the sections blocked below. The rule is "cite us, do not
# train on us": an agent that fetches a page to answer a question and names the
# source sends a prospective buyer back, and it reads live prices instead of
# reciting a stale snapshot. See DEV-7718.
User-agent: *
# -- answer and search engines (fetch to cite, drive referral traffic)
User-agent: OAI-SearchBot
User-agent: ClaudeBot
User-agent: Claude-SearchBot
User-agent: PerplexityBot
User-agent: Applebot
User-agent: Amazonbot
# -- fetchers acting for a live user (a person asked for this page right now,
#    so turning them away is closer to blocking a browser than a crawler)
User-agent: ChatGPT-User
User-agent: Claude-User
User-agent: Perplexity-User
# No blanket "Allow: /" here. It is a no-op for a longest-match parser (nothing
# is disallowed by default) and actively wrong for a first-match one, which
# would read it as "everything allowed" and skip every Disallow below. This
# group is aimed at AI crawlers, whose parsers vary, so the line is left out.

# -- Deliberately not blocked
#    */map* was dropped in DEV-7718. An answer engine should be able to fetch
#    the map search and cite it, and the AI agents above share this group, so
#    allowing it for them is the same as allowing it for everyone. That is the
#    accepted trade: the page keeps itself out of the index without robots.txt,
#    because MapSearchController hardcodes RobotsTag = NO_INDEX on both map
#    actions. llms.txt no longer advertises the map search either (DEV-7724);
#    the list search covers the same inventory, server-rendered.

# -- Language purity: no URL may mix slugs from two languages
#    The route resolves a type, subtype or transaction slug in ANY language
#    under ANY culture prefix, so /nl/vastgoed/maison/a-vendre/gent serves the
#    same results as the Dutch URL and duplicates it.
#
#    This is the ONLY indexing rule robots.txt owns for search and detail URLs.
#    PropertyTypeTree membership, the property type and transaction allow-lists
#    and the excluded combinations are decided by
#    SearchUrlParameters.ToIndexOrNotToIndex and
#    PropertyUrlParameters.ToIndexOrNotToIndex, which emit a meta robots tag.
#    A noindex tag can only be obeyed on a page the crawler may fetch, so
#    blocking those URLs here would hide the very tag that carries the
#    decision. Language purity is the one thing the tag cannot express: the
#    parser resolves a slug in any language, so the mixed URL above parses to
#    House + Sale and the tag says INDEX.
#
#    Three lines per slug: one ending in / for the slug as an inner segment, one
#    ending in $ for a URL that stops at the slug (/en/real-estate/huis), and one
#    ending in ? for that same URL carrying a query string, which the $ anchor
#    does not match (/nl/vastgoed/maison?page=2). A bare prefix would be wrong:
#    /nl/*/land also matches the city Landen and the Dutch slug landbouwgrond.
#
#    GENERATED by tools/generate-language-purity-rules.py from the enums and
#    Resources/DataAnnotations*.resx. Regenerate after adding or renaming a
#    type or transaction label; do not edit by hand.
#
#    -- section words from another language
Disallow: *en/immobilier*
Disallow: *en/vastgoed/*
Disallow: *fr/real-estate/*
Disallow: *fr/vastgoed/*
Disallow: *nl/immobilier*
Disallow: *nl/real-estate*

# =============================================================================
# 3. Googlebot-News: news and article content only
# =============================================================================
User-agent: Googlebot-News
Allow: /fr/article*
Allow: /nl/article*
Allow: /en/article*

Disallow: /

# =============================================================================
# 4. AI crawlers we turn away
# =============================================================================
# Training-only crawlers. They take the content and send nothing back: no
# citation, no referral. Listings are perishable, so a model trained on a
# snapshot quotes prices that were right months ago and attributes them to us.
# The listings are also supplied by agencies and private owners under terms that
# do not contemplate model training, so this is the licensing-safe default.
#
# Google-Extended and Applebot-Extended are robots.txt control tokens, not
# crawlers. Blocking them gates Gemini and Apple Intelligence training only, and
# has NO effect on Google Search or Spotlight indexing.
#
# Note this file is advisory. Bytespider and CCBot honour it inconsistently;
# enforcement is Akamai Bot Manager (DEV-7773), currently on Monitor.
User-agent: GPTBot
User-agent: Google-Extended
User-agent: Applebot-Extended
User-agent: CCBot
User-agent: Bytespider
User-agent: meta-externalagent
Disallow: /
